newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKI JUMPING-THOMA PENALISED BUT TAKES WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-THOMA PENALISED BUT TAKES WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Germany's Dieter Thoma was penalised for sitting on his skis but went top of the World Cup ski jumping standings with a second-place finish on Saturday.

Thoma overtook 17-year-old Primoz Peterka of Slovenia in the standings with jumps of 131 metres and 119.5 metres. The German would have won the high hill event had he not been penalised by two of the five judges.
Austrian Martin Hoellwarth was the winner with jumps of 120 and 126.5 metres.
"It is a rotten thing when you get a great jump (131 metres) and still end up in second place," Thoma said. "I did not land in the snow on that jump."

Two of the five judges ruled his bottom had touched the ground and so called the first jump a crash. His 131-metre effort was nearly five metres further than the second best jump of the day, a 126.5 metre effort by Peterka.
Peterka, who finished third and now trails Thoma by 904 to 892 points, said: "I am going to take first place again soon."
